_note: Readable books, scrolls and inscriptions. Each page lists the knowledge it grants when actually read. Latin lines are classical; translations are kept here and shown under the Latin. Incantation knowledge lets Mika ATTEMPT a spell; only successful practice builds mastery.

pages.heading: Gather, Shape, Release
pages.text: Every spell begins as a breath held in the hands. First gather: draw the loose light of the circle toward you, slowly. Then shape: give it a single clear form, and do not change your mind halfway. Only then release.

pages.heading: Listening to the Circle
pages.text: The circle is not a tool but a listener. Cast gently and it answers with light along its lines; force it and it falls silent. An apprentice who can hold the orb steady for nine heartbeats has begun to listen.

pages.heading: A Note in the Margin
pages.text: Written later, in a smaller hand: 'The orb wakes more than runes. In the west chamber the stone answers it like a heartbeat. I have told no one.  A.'

pages.heading: Where Three Lines Cross
pages.text: Where three ley-lines cross, a circle was cut into the living stone. Speak to it gently and it will answer; force it and it will sleep. Each mage who learns here adds a voice to the circle, and the circle remembers every voice.

keepers_daybook.title: The Keeper's Daybook
keepers_daybook.subtitle: kept by Aurel, last Keeper of the Heartstone

pages.heading: First Entry
pages.text: The Heartstone was quiet again tonight. When the orb is cast in the circle it answers twice, slow, like a sleeper's heart. The old texts say it should answer three times. Something is missing.

latin.translation: The heart of the stone beats three times.

pages.heading: On Memory
pages.text: The Circle's elders taught a saying I did not understand until now. The stone forgets the pattern it was made for, but still water holds whatever light passes through it, if the light is shaped like the sign.

latin.translation: What the stone forgets, the water remembers.

pages.heading: The Sign of Return
pages.text: I have carved the Sign of Return on the stone beside the forest gate, too faint for daylight. It cannot be read, only woken. Whoever wakes it and carries its shape to still water will see what the Heartstone has forgotten.

pages.heading: Last Entry
pages.text: The Circle leaves at dawn. They asked me to bind the Heartstone to sleep, and I have. But I left it a way to wake: a sign, a pond, and a mage patient enough to read. If you are reading this, you are probably that mage. Be kind to it.

pages.heading: Wind and Flame
pages.text: A flame leans away from a gentle wind and steadies again. A shaped gust, strong enough, takes the breath from a flame entirely. Practise on a brazier: the flame will tell you, honestly, how strong your wind has become.

pages.heading: Water and Fire
pages.text: Water called against fire rises as steam and steals its heat. Water called upon water moves in rings; called strongly, it stands up in a column before it falls. Still water is the best teacher: every ring shows your intent.

pages.heading: Two Breaths Together
pages.text: The old mages joined breaths. Water and wind together raise a veil of mist that hides and heals. No apprentice should attempt it before both breaths answer reliably.

pages.heading: The Warding Glyph
pages.text: A ward is a promise drawn in light: four strokes, closed, and held while you breathe out. It turns aside small harms. It is the first glyph every Initiate must be able to draw with their eyes closed.

pages.heading: Signs That Sleep
pages.text: Some signs are carved to be invisible. They are not hidden by depth but by silence: no light has asked them anything for a long time. A woken sign glows along every line it was ever given.

pages.heading: The Waking Word
pages.text: To wake a sign, touch it with a thin line of light, never a blow. An orb will only outline it. The waking word gives the light its edge.

pages.heading: Gathering Power
pages.text: Before a hard spell, stand still and let the elements come to you. It is slow and it looks like nothing, but the next spell you cast will carry more than your own strength.

latin.translation: Powers of the elements, gather in me!

pages.heading: A Practical Receipt: Luminous Draught
pages.text: Into a clean bowl pour moonwater, then a little sylph dew, and stir once with a thread of arcane light. It should glow softly and smell of rain. Never add ember salt to moonwater: it fizzes, smokes and ruins the bowl's patience.

pages.heading: Tablet of the Heartstone
pages.text: The Heartstone was the sanctuary's first relic: a crystal that drinks moonlight and remembers every spell cast within the circle. When the First Circle left, they bound it to sleep.

pages.heading: The Second Inscription
pages.text: Lines that were not there before glow under the first: 'The Circle keeps its oath beneath the southern water. When the stone beats three times, the way to the drowned towers will open to the one who woke it.'

latin.translation: The oath is kept beneath the water.

pages.heading: Inscription on the Forest Gate
pages.text: Leave the noise of the world beyond this arch. Within, the stones remember. (Several later lines have been chiselled away. Only one word survives at the end: REDITUS, return.)

atlas_of_the_ten_rings.title: Atlas of the Ten Rings
atlas_of_the_ten_rings.subtitle: star chart of the Village Observatory, with the keeper's notes

pages.heading: The Lumen and the Hush
pages.text: Before anything, the old charts say, there was the Lumen - a sea of light with no shores - and the Hush, the stillness that light falls into. Where they touched they made a ring of ground, the Orbis, our world. Every spell is a little of the Lumen asked to touch the world again.

pages.heading: Ten Rings of Heaven
pages.text: Round the Orbis lie ten rings of light, the Orbits, one inside the next. A mage climbs them as she grows: the first ring is learned with the breath, the tenth with the whole of oneself. Each ring was first walked by a mortal, and each of those ten became a Warden - the bright knots you can see on clear nights, set along this chart in gold.

pages.heading: Keeper's Note
pages.text: Pencilled in the margin: 'On autumn nights the Twin Lights stand straight above the summit temple for an hour after midnight. The summit-folk say that is when the ninth ring can be heard. I have climbed four times and heard only wind. - E.'

wardens_of_the_orbits.title: On the Wardens of the Orbits
wardens_of_the_orbits.subtitle: the rare grimoire of the Great Library

pages.heading: Aelis, Warden of the First Ring
pages.text: Aelis was a shepherd who whistled the wind to her flock. She learned that breath given out before a word carries the word further - the first lesson every apprentice still learns. Her ring is the ring of breath; its gate opens to those who can hold the light steady for nine heartbeats.

pages.heading: Verdance and Umbra
pages.text: The third Warden, Verdance, grew a forest in a single night to hide a village from a fire; the Sylvan arts descend from her. The fourth, Umbra, was a lamplighter who learned the shapes of shadow and kept the dark from swallowing a city; the Umbral arts descend from him. The old masters held that Sylvan and Umbral mages are drawn to each other the way root is drawn to shade.

pages.heading: Emberhart and the Stonefather
pages.text: Emberhart, fifth, went into a burning mountain and came out as a bird of flame; the phoenixes, it is said, are his sparks. The Stonefather, sixth, sang to the deep rock until it grew crystal, and built the hollow sentinels to keep what he buried. Do not wake his sentinels without need.

pages.heading: The Weaver, the Mirror Queen, the Twins and the Crown
pages.text: The seventh Warden, the Weaver of Ways, learned to fold the distance between two places like cloth; her glyphs are carved on old shrine stones in the deep forests, and no one has read them whole. The eighth, the Mirror Queen, saw the same moment from both sides. The ninth ring belongs to two at once - the Skyborn Twins, sisters who would not climb without each other. The tenth is the Crown: no Warden holds it; it is held by whoever has heard all nine.

founders_plaque.title: The Founder's Plaque
founders_plaque.subtitle: bronze, on the fountain statue of the Academy courtyard

pages.heading: Ilvane of the Circle
pages.text: THIS ACADEMY WAS RAISED BY ILVANE, LAST APPRENTICE OF THE FIRST CIRCLE, WHO WOULD NOT LET WHAT THE CIRCLE KNEW SLEEP WITH THE HEARTSTONE. LEARN IN THE OPEN. TEACH WHAT YOU ARE TAUGHT. AND WHEN YOU CLIMB, LOOK DOWN NOW AND THEN AT WHO IS CLIMBING BEHIND YOU.

shrine_glyph_stones.title: Glyph Stones of the Forgotten Shrine
shrine_glyph_stones.subtitle: runic script, worn by rain
shrine_glyph_stones.location: Forgotten Forest Shrine, the standing stones

pages.heading: The First Stone
pages.text: (The runes are the old script; with care they read:) 'Two places are two folds of one cloth. The Weaver does not travel. She brings the folds together and steps across the seam.'

pages.heading: The Second Stone
pages.text: 'Know both places as you know your own hands: the ground, the light, the sound of each. A fold made to a place half-known tears.' Below, smaller and newer: 'The Weaver's own words were never carved here. They are said to sleep under the summit, where the ninth ring is heard.'

vault_inscription.title: The Vault Inscription
vault_inscription.subtitle: carved beside the door of the Ancient Vault
vault_inscription.location: Deep Caverns, beside the vault door

pages.heading: Sealed by the Stonefather's Makers
pages.text: 'Here the makers of the sentinels laid down what they could not unmake. The seal answers crystal, not force. Whoever opens it: the sentinels were made to keep this place, not to hate you. Speak to them as keepers.'

summit_frieze.title: Frieze of the Cloud Temple
summit_frieze.subtitle: carved round the inner wall of the summit temple
summit_frieze.location: Celestial Summit, inside the Cloud Temple

pages.heading: The Twins Who Would Not Climb Alone
pages.text: Two sisters climb a stair of clouds, one carrying a branch in leaf, the other a lamp. At the ninth step the stair splits; each may go on alone, faster. They sit down where the stair splits and wait for each other, and the stair joins again under them. Over their heads the carvers cut two stars.

pages.heading: Under the Stars
pages.text: An inscription below the stars, in the old script: 'The ninth gate is not opened by one. Come when the Twin Lights stand over this roof.'

village_notices.title: Village Notice Board
village_notices.subtitle: pinned papers, some new, some rained on

pages.heading: Notices
pages.text: FRESH BREAD before the eighth bell at Hilde's stall - and honey cakes on market days.  /  Lost: one good iron hammer. Bram.  /  Wolves seen past the river road - travel in daylight. Captain Rook, the Watch.  /  Wenna buys moonpetal and glowcap, fair prices.

pages.heading: Older Papers
pages.text: A faded one: 'The Academy's open lessons are held on the east lawn in the mornings. Visitors may sit at the back if they are quiet. - M. Aldric.' Another, nearly washed away: '...the observatory keeper asks that anyone who hears music on the summit at night write it down for her...'

weaver_words.title: The Weaver's Words
weaver_words.subtitle: a stone set in the floor beneath the Cloud Temple's altar
weaver_words.location: Celestial Summit, beneath the temple altar

pages.heading: Two Folds of One Cloth
pages.text: 'Stand where you are and see where you would be. Hold both as one: the ground under each foot, the light on each stone. When they are one in you, they are one in the world. Then do not walk - cross.'

pages.heading: The Word
pages.text: 'Say it once, and only to a place your eyes hold. What you cannot see you do not know, and what you do not know will not fold.'
